intro: This week’s intelligence digest highlights key developments across retail, luxury, and AI sectors, including Amazon’s new surcharge amid rising logistics costs and Anthropic’s strategic expansion through acquisitions and political engagement. readOneThing.title: Amazon to issue 3.5% surcharge on fulfillment services as fuel, logistics costs rise

items.title: Amazon to issue 3.5% surcharge on fulfillment services as fuel, logistics costs rise
bullets: Amazon will implement a 3.5% surcharge on fulfillment fees for merchants using Fulfillment by Amazon in the U.S., Canada, and some cross-border services starting April 17, 2026.
The surcharge will average about $0.17 per unit in the U.S. and is calculated on fulfillment fees rather than the sale price of items.
This temporary fee increase follows similar surcharges in 2022 and reflects rising fuel costs due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and disruptions in key shipping routes.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: Starting April 17, Amazon will add a 3.5% surcharge on merchants' fulfillment fees due to increased fuel and logistics costs driven by Middle East conflicts, impacting supply chains.

items.title: An exception to luxury’s slowed growth, Perigold eyes vacant department store locations amid expansion
bullets: Perigold, launched by Wayfair as its luxury counterpart, is expanding through physical stores and content collaborations despite a slowing luxury market.
In 2025, Perigold opened its first two stores in Houston and West Palm Beach, with store sizes ranging from 20,000 to 30,000 square feet.
Perigold's customer base includes affluent consumers across California, Texas, and the East Coast, with a growing B2B segment and plans for further category expansion.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: Perigold, launched by Wayfair as its luxury counterpart, is expanding despite the luxury sector's slowed growth, having opened its first two stores in Houston and West Palm Beach in 2025 and recently investing in a major collaboration.

items.title: Mejuri builds on its fastest-selling collection, with most shoppers buying 3 products
bullets: Mejuri expanded its Puzzle collection by introducing sterling silver options and modular slider charms for necklaces, enabling over 16 million combinations.
Sixty percent of customers purchase three or more Puzzle stacking rings at once, making it the brand's fastest-selling product to date.
The Puzzle collection launch followed rising gold prices and increased demand for affordable materials like sterling silver and vermeil since last year.

items.title: New Ecommerce Tools: April 1, 2026
bullets: Designkit launched an AI-powered platform that generates complete product image sets from a single prompt, supporting batch processing and localization in five languages.
FedEx Office now offers Amazon's free, label-free, box-free return option at over 1,500 U.S. locations, simplifying the return process for eligible items.
Shopify merchants can sell products through ChatGPT and other generative AI platforms using Shopify's Agentic Storefronts, integrating AI sales channels centrally from the Shopify admin.

items.title: Anthropic ramps up its political activities with a new PAC
bullets: Anthropic has filed documents to establish a new political action committee called AnthroPAC to influence policy and regulation during the midterm elections.
AnthroPAC will be funded by voluntary employee contributions capped at $5,000 and plans to donate to both current lawmakers and rising political candidates.
This political move comes as AI companies have contributed $185 million to midterm races, and Anthropic is involved in a legal dispute with the Defense Department over AI model usage.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: Anthropic has launched a new political action committee (PAC) aimed at supporting candidates aligned with its AI policy agenda ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.

items.title: Women’s Jewelry Association Launches Jewelry & Watches Mentorship Cohort With Mentoro
bullets: The Women’s Jewelry Association and Mentoro launched a Jewelry & Watches mentorship cohort at an event held on March 26 in New York City.
The program features workshops led by industry experts and includes three dedicated one-on-one mentor-mentee sessions for participants.
The launch event included remarks from industry leaders and a panel discussion, emphasizing the legacy of women in leadership within the jewelry sector.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: The Women’s Jewelry Association partnered with Mentoro to launch a mentorship cohort, matching mentors and mentees across key fields during a March 26 event in New York. This initiative aims to support professionals in the jewellery industry.

items.title: Aldi taps Instacart to power its U.S. website
bullets: Instacart's platform enables better product recommendations, shoppable recipes, and seamless shopping experiences, leading to higher engagement and basket size.
Since 2017, Aldi has partnered with Instacart for same-day delivery and now uses its exclusive digital fulfillment platform amid plans to open over 180 new stores in 31 states in 2026.
